observations.finding: Observed a flexed support leg and forward/lateral trunk at plant, opposite arm extension and hip/trunk rotation at release, then a recovery support change. This is a qualitative single-kick 2D study, not calibrated 3D capture or evidence for every football action.

Predicted pose error, relative velocity and implicit damping act through articulated mass/inertia. Retain bounded parent-relative muscular torques; soften the supported response without reducing player mass or unbinding joints.

Damping and stiffness determine settling and continuity. Counter-tilt and support response retain damping near critical with lower stiffness; do not slow the simulation or restart the response each frame.
Balance couples centre-of-mass velocity, capture point and feasible support polygon; the foot must move into reachable support instead of applying arbitrary whole-body translation.

implementation: An incoming central foot reception may be evaluated by the real-skin solver instead of failing only the old proxy marker. Fixed-length leg reach can lower the pelvis by at most 5.5 cm while pinning the opposite ankle; selection and live pose use the same curve.
Clear the previous action and per-actor reach on position resets. Recognize the best nearby CPU receiver throughout the 1.2-second prediction horizon, avoiding an early chase before a high arrival.

Counter-tilt stiffness 144 to 100 and damping 24 to 20; support stiffness 100 to 81 and damping 20 to 18. Slightly more dynamic torso/arm contribution under actual load with existing anatomical projections.

Index immutable contact vertices, bind-local weights and triangle part groups. Reuse only thread-local per-query posed vertices, preserving the original nearest-triangle distance comparison and skin contact tolerances.
Use 12 solver iterations for quiet active tracking and 24 under load; free-fall worlds retain 40 iterations. Keep 100 Hz and both substeps.

Plan charged cross/through distance with reference drag, bounce and rolling resistance, then constrain native release-power variation to eight percent while preserving direction and measured contact spin.
limitations: The external journal article and PDF returned HTTP 403; their contents were not treated as retrieved research.
No new captured 3D animations or full-body reinforcement-learning policy were created. The shipped reduced learned balance and angular muscle controllers remain unchanged.
A reference range model does not model every turf patch or contact spin; actual match flight remains the live ball integrator.
This is a bounded hybrid active-body prototype, not a reproduction of the proprietary Euphoria system or exact player-specific motion.
